description: Issue #838 AC2, the headline: a program may not DECLARE a built-in name, and the profile set it runs under has nothing to do with it. Every `define` below was measured CLEAN at the saga tip `fc4371d` under this exact Core-only profile set, which is the set a beginner's program runs under -- so `define forward` was accepted and the turtle then silently stopped moving, with zero diagnostics at any stage. Five names, chosen to cover the five ways a name reaches the rule: `forward` is a Turtle & Rendering canonical, `fd` is a Heritage short alias resolving to it (blocked BY CONSTRUCTION, through `canonicalOfHeritageAlias`, never a parallel list), `setxy` is one of the five compact alias spellings that share a table entry with `set_xy` and used to create a call-site-dependent split with no diagnostic at either end, `hint` is an Educational meta-command, and `challenge` is Tutor's one command -- which before this slice had no registry at all. `spec/grammar.md:382` ("`define count`, `define forward`, and `define fd` are equally errors"), `:408` ("what a profile decides is whether a name *works*, never whether a program may declare it") and `:414` (built-in names are versioned with the specification, so an implementation "MUST reject a declaration of exactly that version's built-in names"). Core-only is the assertion that matters here: a fixture run under the full DAG would pass even for an implementation that gated these names per profile. `"check": true` -- a checker rule, nothing is executed and no events are produced.
